Medieval knights used a variety of weapons in battle, including swords, spears, axes, maces, bows and arrows, crossbows, polearms, and daggers.

The armor worn by medieval knights had a significant impact on their weapon choices.

Plate armor was the most effective type of armor in the medieval period, consisting of a suit of interlocking metal plates that covered the entire body.

Knights often used weapons that could deliver powerful blows to penetrate plate armor, such as heavy maces, hammers, or battle axes.
Chainmail was a lighter option than plate armor, consisting of interlocking rings of metal that covered the body.
Chainmail was less protective than plate armor but allowed greater mobility.
Knights wearing chainmail would often use quicker and more agile weapons, such as swords or spears.
Leather armor was the most basic form of armor used in the medieval period, consisting of thick leather that provided some protection against bladed weapons.
Knights wearing leather armor would often use ranged weapons such as bows and arrows or crossbows.
